findings.description:
Logical AND is used instead of logical OR when verifying team admin or owner permissions. — WHAT: Logical AND (`&&`) is used instead of logical OR (`||`) when checking `isTeamAdminOrOwner`.
WHY: A user who is either a team admin or a team owner (but not simultaneously both) evaluates to `false`, causing authorized team admins or owners to be denied access with a FORBIDDEN error.
HOW: Replace `&&` with `||` so that having either the admin or owner role grants permission.

Unescaped hyphen in `[a-zA-Z-_]` creates an ASCII range matching path separators, causing directory corruption on paths with underscores. — WHAT: The character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` treats `-_` as a character range from `-` (ASCII 45) to `_` (ASCII 95), which matches path separators (`/` and `\`) and is not anchored to the end of the path.
WHY: If any directory in the absolute file path contains an underscore (e.g., `/workspace/keycloak_dev/...`), `replaceAll` matches from that directory's underscore across path separators up to `.properties`, replacing the entire tail with `_en.properties` and causing a runtime `FileNotFoundException`.
HOW: Escape the hyphen or place it at the end of the character class (e.g. `[a-zA-Z_\\-]`) and anchor the match to the end of the string with `$`.

Unbounded `end` calculation can cause `start + end > length`, throwing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` during diff formatting. — WHAT: The `end` matching loop does not bound `end` by `sanitized.length() - start` and `value.length() - start`. WHY: When `value` and `sanitized` share identical characters at both the start and end (for example repeated tags like `

` sanitized to `
`), `start + end` can exceed the length of the string, causing `sanitized.length() - end < start` and throwing a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `substring(start, length - end)`. HOW: Bound the `end` loop condition with `end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start`.

localCache caches failed device tagging attempts, allowing rejected anonymous devices to bypass the device limit on subsequent requests — WHAT: tagDeviceUI caches the device key in localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, leaving failed or rejected device tags cached.
WHY: When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the request is rejected, but the device key remains cached in localCache for 29 minutes; any subsequent request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil from TagDevice, and successfully authenticates as anonymous, completely bypassing the device limit.
HOW: Move localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) in tagDeviceUI so it is only called after anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or delete the key from localCache if CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error.

Rejected anonymous devices remain cached in localCache, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests. — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` inserts the device cache key into `localCache` before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, without evicting the key if `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error.
WHY: When a device exceeds the limit and `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the device key remains cached for 29 minutes, causing all subsequent requests from that device to hit `localCache.Get`, return `nil`, and bypass the device limit check.
HOW: Update `tagDeviceUI` to set `localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` only after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` returns successfully (or delete the key from `localCache` on error).

Calling scrub on i.content raises NoMethodError when polling RSS feeds that do not have a content tag — WHAT: Calling `i.content.scrub` throws `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` when polling feeds where `i.content` is nil.
WHY: SimpleRSS maps `<description>` to `i.description` and standard RSS 2.0 feeds do not have `<content>` tags, causing the scheduled `PollFeed` job to crash immediately on any RSS 2.0 feed.
HOW: Fall back to `i.description` (or `i.content_encoded`) if `i.content` is nil, and guard against nil before calling `.scrub`.

SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase raises NoMethodError if the setting is blank — WHAT: `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` is called without guarding against `embed_by_username` being nil or blank.
WHY: If the `embed_by_username` site setting is not configured, attempting to retrieve topics will crash with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'downcase' for nil:NilClass`.
HOW: Check `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` before calling `.downcase`.

Mutating contents in-place with `<<` raises NoMethodError if contents is nil — WHAT: `contents << ...` mutates `contents` in place without guarding against `contents` being nil.
WHY: When `import_remote` fails to parse a document's content, `doc.content` can be `nil`, causing `contents << ...` to raise `NoMethodError: undefined method '<<' for nil:NilClass`.
HOW: Reassign `contents` using string interpolation instead of in-place mutation.

Storage creation failure records legacy duration metrics instead of storage duration metrics. — WHAT: recordLegacyDuration is called when d.Storage.Create fails.
WHY: Storage failure metrics are attributed to Legacy storage duration metrics, causing misleading metric reporting and concealing unified store error rates.
HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration to d.recordStorageDuration.

Storage update failure records legacy duration metrics instead of storage duration metrics. — WHAT: recordLegacyDuration is called when d.Storage.Update fails.
WHY: Storage failure metrics are attributed to Legacy storage duration metrics, corrupting metric dashboards and alerting for update operations.
HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration to d.recordStorageDuration.

Legacy delete collection records storage duration metrics instead of legacy duration metrics. — WHAT: recordStorageDuration is called to record the asynchronous Legacy delete collection operation duration.
WHY: Legacy delete-collection execution times and errors are recorded under the unified Storage metrics instead of Legacy metrics.
HOW: Change d.recordStorageDuration to d.recordLegacyDuration.

Delete operation records object name instead of resource kind as metric label. — WHAT: The object name parameter is passed as the kind label argument to recordStorageDuration.
WHY: Using unique resource names instead of resource kinds leads to unbounded metric label cardinality in Prometheus and inconsistent metric series.
HOW: Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration.

Delete method sets un-annotated logger on context instead of contextual logger. — WHAT: d.Log is passed to klog.NewContext instead of log.
WHY: Downstream storage calls extracting the logger from ctx will lack the structured name, kind, and method attributes attached to log.
HOW: Pass log instead of d.Log to klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

Asynchronous legacy operations use request context directly and get cancelled when HTTP request completes. — WHAT: Asynchronous goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the incoming request ctx.
WHY: When the parent HTTP request handler finishes and returns the response, the request context is cancelled, causing the asynchronous legacy storage write to be immediately aborted.
HOW: Detach context cancellation from the parent request context (e.g., using context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before applying the 10-second timeout.
